This Age
this ayj
noun phrase
From the Greek ai&omacr;n houtos, “this age” or “this present world,” the evil order of things from which Christ delivers, set against ho ai&omacr;n ho mell&omacr;n, “the age to come.”

📖 Biblical Definition

This age is the Scripture’s name for the present evil order of the world, fallen under sin and the prince of the power of the air, from which Christ gave Himself to deliver His people. He gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father (Gal 1:4). It is set in plain contrast with the age to come, for God hath set His Son far above all principality and power, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come (Eph 1:21); and the sin against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven, neither in this world, neither in the world to come (Mat 12:32). This age has its own wisdom, its own princes that come to nought, its own fashion that passeth away; and the grace of God teaches us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world (Tit 2:12). The dictionary marks that this age is not a neutral span of time but a moral order opposed to God, the kingdom of darkness over which the god of this world holds his usurped dominion. The believer lives in it but is not of it, a pilgrim and a stranger passing through, set free by the cross from its bondage and its doom, and waiting for the age to come, the everlasting kingdom of the Lord Jesus Christ, in which dwelleth righteousness.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The present evil order of the world, from which Christ delivers, set against the age to come.

expand to see more

THIS AGE, the present evil order of the world, also called this present world.

Christ gave Himself to deliver His people from this present evil world.

It is set in contrast with the age, or world, to come.

It has its own wisdom, its princes, and its fashion that passeth away.

It witnesses to the believer as a pilgrim, in this age but not of it.

📖 Key Scripture

Gal 1:4 — "Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father:"

Eph 1:21 — "Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come:"

Mat 12:32 — "And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come."

Tit 2:12 — "Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The spirit of this age presses conformity upon the church, and the love of this present world draws even professors away.

expand to see more

This age has always had its lovers, and the present hour is no exception. The progressive temper of the times bids the church measure herself by the changing fashions of this present world, to baptize its passing wisdom and conform her doctrine to its shifting standards, until the line between the church and the age is all but rubbed away. Of one such lover the apostle wrote with grief, Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world (2Ti 4:10); and the same draught draws professors still, who would have the name of Christ and the friendship of the age together.

The dictionary answers with the apostle’s charge, Be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind (Rom 12:2). The fashion of this age passeth away, and its wisdom is foolishness with God; the friendship of the world is enmity with God. The recovery is the pilgrim mind that lives in this age as a stranger and not a citizen, set free by the cross from the present evil world, refusing to be squeezed into its mould, and waiting in holiness for the age to come, wherein dwelleth righteousness.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “this present world,” this age names the evil order Christ delivers from, set against the age to come.

expand to see more

This Age — Greek ai&omacr;n houtos, “this age” or “this present world.”

It stands against ho ai&omacr;n ho mell&omacr;n, “the age to come.”

Christ gave Himself to deliver us from this present evil world.

It has its own wisdom and fashion, which passeth away.

The believer lives in it as a pilgrim, not of it.

Usage

"Like the pilgrim in this present evil age, the believer lives within it as a stranger and not a citizen."

"Demas loved this present world and forsook the apostle; the same draught draws professors still."

"Be not conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewing of the mind, waiting for the age to come."
